tracking.name: Global Shield against Climate Risks
tracking.description: The Global Shield provides and facilitates more and better pre-arranged protection against climate- and disaster-related risks for vulnerable people and countries, enabling greater financial protection and faster, more reliable preparedness and response to loss and damage.
tracking.indicator: More Countries/Regions with Pre-Arranged Protection Against Climate and Disaster-Related Risks
tracking.findings: By the end of 2025, the Global Shield In-Country Process had been carried out in 14 countries. Through its financing vehicles, Global Shield Financing Facility enabled 17 countries to access financial protection, directly protecting 4.2 million people, including 2.3 million women, while Global Shield Solutions Platform reported 4.8 million vulnerable people protected under its global and regional thematic windows.

tracking.name: Net-Zero Export Credit Agencies Alliance (NZECA)
tracking.description: The member-led and UN-convened Net-Zero Export Credit Agencies Alliance (NZECA) unites leading public trade finance institutions committed to delivering net-zero economies by 2050 by supporting the decarbonisation of trade and facilitating joint action from public and private finance.
tracking.indicator: Number of members with publicly available intermediate and net-zero by 2050
tracking.findings: Five full members set and publicly disclosed an intermediate science-based target for 2030 or sooner, consistent with a pathway to net zero by 2050 at the latest.

tracking.name: Sustainable Business COP
tracking.description: A permanent business platform with representatives from more than 120 countries and territories, reaching over 55 million companies. It mobilizes the private sector to implement the Paris Agreement and deliver the 1.5°C goal across the six axes of the Global Climate Action Agenda.
tracking.indicator: Permanent business platform at UNFCCC COPs
tracking.findings: Sustainable Business COP reached representatives from more than 120 countries and territories by August 2026, up from more than 60 in September 2025, surpassing the target of 100.

cases.title: Strengthening institutional capacity for climate and disaster risk finance
cases.initiative: by the Global Shield against Climate Risks
cases.target: Related CCI target: More Countries/Regions with Pre-Arranged Protection Against Climate and Disaster-Related Risks
cases.contribution: This action is reported as contributing to Objective 20. Climate, sustainable and adaptation finance, mainstreaming climate in investments and insurance, and Objective 26. Governance, state capacities and institutional strengthening for climate action, planning and preparedness (under Axis 6).
body: The Global Shield strengthens the technical and institutional capacity needed to develop and implement effective Climate and Disaster Risk Finance and Insurance (CDRFI) solutions. Through the Global Shield Solutions Platform (GSSP), partner countries and regional actors receive capacity-development support linked to climate risk analysis, research and education, and the design and implementation of financial protection solutions. GSSP also promotes knowledge exchange and collaboration among CDRFI practitioners and regional risk pools. The Global Shield Financing Facility (GSFF) complements this work through country and regional training, workshops and knowledge exchanges that strengthen government and stakeholder capabilities in areas including CDRFI analytics, risk modelling, financial protection and shock-responsive systems.

These activities contribute to the Global Shield's goal of closing financial protection gaps by strengthening the knowledge, technical expertise and institutional capabilities required to make informed risk-financing decisions and implement CDRFI solutions. Building these capabilities supports more sustained country and regional ownership of financial protection approaches and strengthens the enabling conditions for CDRFI solutions to be designed, implemented and maintained over time.

In 2025, GSSP convened 64 experts at the third Climate Risk Finance Forum, supporting technical exchange on sustainable premium and capital support, and GSFF conducted 25 workshops, trainings and exchanges reaching 585 participants across multiple regions. Activities covered areas including CDRFI analytics, flood modelling, digital disaster risk management platforms and de-risking livestock value chains, alongside regional workshops and knowledge exchanges supporting peer learning and collaboration. GSFF also produced and disseminated 42 CDRFI knowledge and analytical products to strengthen the evidence base available to governments and practitioners.

cases.title: Systematizing Export Credit Agencies’ GHG Accounting Practices
cases.initiative: by the Net-Zero Export Credit Agencies Alliance (NZECA)
cases.target: Related CCI target: Number of members with publicly available intermediate and net-zero by 2050
body: The initiative advances GHG accounting methodologies for Export Credit Agencies (ECAs) by convening online workshops with NZECA members. Insights generated will contribute to an internal white paper and support the evolution of future Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials (PCAF) standards that more accurately reflect the activities and financing structures of ECAs.

Through the development of practical and applicable GHG accounting practices for ECAs, combined with annual reporting of individual and collective progress, this initiative strengthens transparency and accountability in the sector. The resulting insights and disclosures support enhanced transparency frameworks and help align ECA activities with long-term low-GHG development strategies and the climate policy objectives of their home countries and the Paris Agreement.

cases.title: Sustainable Business COP Awards
body: Sustainable Business COP is a strategic initiative backed by 40+ countries. It mobilizes the private sector to deliver the 1.5°C goal, focusing on eight priority areas for a just, resilient, and regenerative economy, including Energy, Bioeconomy, Green Skills, and Transition Finance.

Sustainable Business COP ran a global public call for private sector climate solutions across its eight thematic areas. More than 1,400 submissions were received from organizations worldwide, covering a portfolio of 670 initiatives.

The Working Groups assessed submissions on scale of impact, feasibility within five years, economic viability, innovation and alignment with Sustainable Business COP priorities. The 48 selected cases from +13 countries, announced in October 2025 and awarded around COP 30 in Belém, showcased private sector implementation aligned with the Global Stocktake outcomes and the objectives of the Global Climate Action Agenda.

These cases show that scalable private sector climate solutions already exist across sectors and regions. They inform Sustainable Business COP recommendations and give COP Presidencies and partners a portfolio of proven solutions for replication and scale.
